properties.via: Les Planches–Le Pont de la Tine
properties.abstract: This circular hike is based around three historical bridges: starting with Pont des Planches, built in 1778, there follows one road-rail bridge and the stone bridge of Pont de la Tine. The trail – which passes through woodland, a ravine and meadows – also features the church at Cergnat with its ancient belfry.
properties.description:
The hike sets off from Le Sépey. Past the Les Plans district, you will get glimpses of the towers of Leysin, the peak of the Grand Chamossaire and the Pic Chaussy along the way. After that, you will see Les Planches bridge, a road-rail bridge. First however, a beautiful path descends into the woods leading to the old bridge of Pont des Planches, located downhill from the railway bridge. It is situated in the wonderful gorge of the Le Grande Eau river and was restored between 2023 to 2024 as the walls were at risk of collapsing. 

Les Planches (Aigle) must be crossed to get from La Forclaz to Le Sépey. Originally, even the main connection from Lake Geneva or the Great St. Bernard pass into the Pays d’Enhaut or to Saanen led through here. Due to the cantonal road that was built between 1836 and 1838 on the right bank of the Le Grande Eau river, Les Planches lost its significance. 

The climb through the woods to the railway bridge is brief but athletically demanding. The view back to the first bridge of Les Planches with the Pic Chaussy in the background is a good photo opportunity. The trail now runs alongside the railway line for a while before descending into the woods, where you will find the third bridge of the route, the Pont de la Tine. Meister Walen reconstructed the bridge in 1729 in the Romanesque style with stone arches. Five years prior, he had built the Napoleon bridge in Aigle. A surfaced road leads past the hydroelectric power station. 

Now comes the longest ascent of the hike: around multiple bends along the cantonal road, through the woods and meadows until you reach the village of Cergnat. In this area, you can visit the 13th century church. It combines architectural elements from various epochs. Inside the ancient tower with its stone spire, there are three beautiful Gothic bells. The final descent to where you set off will be along another forest trail.
properties.title: Sentier des ponts historiques du Sépey
